text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Danes do not seem to invest enough money in small companies compared to the number of investments made in small companies abroad. A new trade ministry proposal is therefore to allow new types of investment associations which should make it easier for private investors to place money in small companies.

--- With the Netherlands and Canada, Denmark is now developing new concepts for United Nations peacekeeping forces, among them a special New York-based rapid reaction force command, charged with planning future missions.

In a crisis the command would be relocated to the field from where it would direct operations. Other proposals involve standardised battalion structures and training and the permanent attachment of an African officer to the task force command.
--- The environment ministry is to grant 18 million crowns for so called green guides which are to advise Danes who want to improve environmental conditions where they live.

--- Small Danish airline Cimber Air is entering the fight for domestic passengers with plans to establish a new route between Aarhus, Denmark's second largest city, and Aalborg, both in western Denmark.
--- A new consumer magazine survey shows that small banks give four times higher interest rates on common deposits than large banks.
